root_idea.summary: The root denotes bending or inclining, especially the bending of a person or other thing.
root_idea.development: From bodily bending and lowering the head, the lexical range extends to the ritual bowing of prayer, humility and self-abasement, prayer itself, thanksgiving prostration, and several physical or figurative applications.

senses.definition: To bow down in the prescribed posture of prayer.
senses.usage_conditions: A bodily act of worship involving the lowering or bending of the body; the Quranic forms include commands to bow and an imperfect statement about bowing.

senses.definition: To humble or abase oneself before God in worship.
senses.usage_conditions: This is an attitudinal extension of bodily bowing, expressing submission or reverence in a worship context.

senses.definition: To pray or join those engaged in prayer.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quran-attested construction interprets the verb with مَعَ الرَّاكِعِينَ as joining those who pray.

senses.definition: One who bows; in worship, one performing the ritual bowing posture of prayer.
senses.usage_conditions: The active participle can describe a person engaged in prayer; Quranic occurrences use it for worshippers characterized by bowing.

senses.definition: One who prostrates himself in thanksgiving.
senses.usage_conditions: A Quran-attested interpretation of the participle describes a person falling into prostration as an act of thanksgiving.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To bend or become bent, lower the head, or fall upon the face and stumble.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This broad physical use includes a person becoming bent through age and the consequences of lowering the head.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To humble or abase oneself in a devotional or other non-ritual context.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A figurative extension of bodily bending; it may describe a humbled person or a lowered state without denoting the prescribed prayer posture.
A reported conventional use referring particularly to taking up the standing position for prayer.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of camels, to become fatigued or languid from fatigue, lowering the head and falling on the face.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized usage describing extreme fatigue or languor in camels.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a palm tree, to incline.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Reported as a possible classical tropical expression; its classical attestation is noted as uncertain.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a man, to become poor after richness, competence, or sufficiency.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression figuratively describes a person's condition becoming lowered or abased.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A single cycle of prayer consisting of standing followed by bowing and two prostrations; by extension, a prayer comprising one such cycle.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plural is رَكَعَاتٌ; the term is also used in expressions for performing one or more prayer cycles.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A deep hollow in the ground.
Bowing or bending; of a person or thing, lowering the head or falling upon the face after lowering it.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The participle may describe either a person or another thing exhibiting this physical posture.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A follower of the true religion who does not worship idols.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A usage attributed to Arab usage in the pre-Islamic period.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of a camel, lowering the head and falling upon the face from fatigue or languor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized participial use for camels affected by extreme fatigue.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A place in which one bows or bends, especially in prayer.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A place-noun use; its plural is مَرَاكِعُ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A hard, long stone upon which wheat or the like is ground.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal use; its plural is مَرَاكِعُ.

cautions: The Quranic nominal group is morphologically an active participle and is presented under the singular citation form رَاكِعٌ, although its supplied occurrences include plural and inflected forms.

The thanksgiving-prostration interpretation is accompanied by a printed Lane citation to chapter 38, verse 23; the example here uses only the independently supplied QAC occurrence 38:24:31, where رَاكِعًا occurs.
